**PR #3734** (DRAFT, auto-merge NOT enabled) · https://github.com/iscasasola/setnayan-platform/pull/3734
Branch `fix/sec6-nsfw-verdict-binding` · worktree `/Users/icecasasola/setnayan-wt-sec6`

## What changed

**Root cause:** the verdict lived inside `events.std_media`, a column the host must be able to write. RLS is row-level, the anon key is public, so `PATCH …{"std_media":{"type":"video","videoKey":"…","nsfw":"approved"}}` bypassed `saveAllStdContent` entirely.

1. **Verdict moved out of the host's reach** — new `events.std_media_nsfw` (`supabase/migrations/20271007493007_events_std_media_nsfw_verdict.sql`), REVOKEd UPDATE/INSERT from `authenticated`+`anon`, `GRANT SELECT` to `authenticated` (builder badge), service-role write only. `StdMedia` no longer *has* an `nsfw` field, so a forged one is unrepresentable; the migration strips the legacy key from every existing blob. No verdict backfilled (backfilling `approved` would bless a forgery — prod has exactly 1 STD video, verified read-only: 1 video, 1 approved, 1 with poster).
2. **Verdict bound to the media** — stores `videoKey`, `posterKey`, and `<etag>:<bytes>` of **both** objects. `stdVideoIsLive` (pure, `lib/std-media.ts`) requires key match; `stdVideoIsServable` (`lib/std-video-gate.ts`, new) re-HEADs and compares fingerprints before serving. Key identity alone is insufficient — `/api/upload` gives a 5-min presigned PUT for a server-chosen key and the screen lands in seconds, so bytes can be swapped under an approved key. No trigger: a host PATCHing around the action invalidates their own approval.
3. **Fail closed everywhere** — missing/malformed verdict, unreadable R2, unknown bucket, absent ETag all deny. Every verdict read is its own query so a deploy landing ahead of the migration degrades to "not approved" instead of 42703-ing `/[slug]` into a 404.
4. `lib/r2.ts` `r2Head` gained one additive `etag` field. `lib/uploads.ts` and the presign paths untouched (SEC-1).

## VERDICT: BROKEN

The **privilege half is genuinely solid** — I attacked it hard and could not move it. The **binding half is bypassable**: the fingerprint is computed against a different resource than the one the guest's browser fetches, so an attacker can get a real `approved` verdict for a decoy object while serving arbitrary unscreened video.

---

## Concrete bypasses

### BYPASS 1 — parser divergence: the fingerprint verifies an R2 object, the browser fetches a foreign origin (defeats the new control)

Two different parsers read the same `videoKey` string:

- **Verify side** — `/Users/icecasasola/setnayan-wt-sec6/apps/web/lib/std-video-gate.ts:109-113` → `parseR2Ref` (`apps/web/lib/nsfw-screen.ts:190-194`): anything without an `r2://` prefix becomes `{bucket:null, key:<whole string>}` and is HEADed **as a key in `setnayan-media`**.
- **Serve side** — `apps/web/app/[slug]/_lib/loaders.ts:324` → `displayUrlForStoredAsset` → `parseStoredAsset` (`apps/web/lib/uploads.ts:59-61`): anything without an `r2://` prefix is returned **verbatim as a URL**, rendered raw at `apps/web/app/[slug]/_components/save-the-date-film.tsx:1680` (`<video src={content.videoUrl}>`).

A string can satisfy both. `sanitizePathPrefix` (`apps/web/app/api/upload/route.ts:185-194`) only strips leading/trailing slashes, drops empty/`.`/`..` segments and rejoins with `/` — it does not reject a scheme segment, and there is no user/event scoping on the generic branch (`route.ts:465-493`). Object key = `${pathPrefix}/${randomUUID()}-${filename}` (`route.ts:566`).

Exploit, as an ordinary authenticated host (no PostgREST needed):

```
1) POST /api/upload
   {"bucket":"media","pathPrefix":"http://evil.example/v",
    "filename":"clip.mp4","contentType":"video/mp4","sizeBytes":2048}
   → r2Key = "http:/evil.example/v/<uuid>-clip.mp4"   // "//" collapsed to "/"
2) PUT 2 KB of a clean mp4 to the returned presigned URL   // the DECOY now exists in R2
3) upload a clean poster JPEG normally → posterKey
4) saveAllStdContent(eventId, { media: { type:'video',
     videoKey:"http:/evil.example/v/<uuid>-clip.mp4", posterKey:<clean poster> } })
```

- `screenStdVideo` → `r2ContentFingerprint` HEADs `setnayan-media/http:/evil.example/v/<uuid>-clip.mp4`, the decoy → real etag+size. Poster classifies clean → **verdict `approved`, bound, fingerprinted.**
- `stdVideoIsServable` re-HEADs the same decoy → **fingerprints match → true.**
- `displayUrlForStoredAsset("http:/evil.example/v/<uuid>-clip.mp4")` → `legacy_url` → returned verbatim.
- Browser: `new URL('http:/evil.example/v/…','https://www.setnayan.com/slug')` → **`http://evil.example/v/…`** (verified with Node's WHATWG parser; the single slash is enough because the scheme differs from the page's — `https:/…` would stay relative, `http:/…` does not). Chrome/Safari auto-upgrade mixed `http:` media to `https:`, so an https-serving attacker host plays fine.
- **CSP does not save this**: `apps/web/next.config.ts:122-126` sets only `frame-ancestors` + `frame-src`. No `default-src`/`media-src`.

Same string flows into `apps/web/app/admin/studio/_surfaces/reveal-studio-surface.tsx:70` — the admin's review player also hits `evil.example`, so the human override can be shown different bytes than guests. Fingerprint binding is verifying the wrong resource.

**Minimal fix:** make both sides use one parser. Require `parseStoredAsset(key).kind === 'r2'` for `videoKey`/`posterKey` inside `resolveStdMedia` (`apps/web/lib/std-media.ts:103`) — a non-`r2://` ref should resolve to `{type:'gallery'}` — and fingerprint via that same resolved `{bucket,key}` rather than `parseR2Ref`'s default-bucket fallback.

### BYPASS 2 — poster substitution: the screened artifact need not come from the video (pre-existing, unaddressed, same outcome)

`saveAllStdContent` (`apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/studio/save-the-date/actions.ts:207-236`) takes `posterKey` straight from the client with no derivation check and no ownership check; the poster is only ever extracted client-side (`apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/_components/std-media-picker.tsx:163-174`). Upload an NSFW mp4 and an unrelated clean JPEG, save them as `{videoKey, posterKey}` — `screenStdVideo` classifies the JPEG, writes `approved`, and the binding is *correct*: it faithfully binds a verdict computed on a cat photo to an NSFW video. Also reachable purely via PostgREST: PATCH `std_media` (still host-writable, correctly so) then load the builder once to trigger the opportunistic heal at `save-the-date/page.tsx:155-161`.

Pre-existing and honestly documented in `nsfw-screen.ts:533-535`, but it means "NSFW filter … CANNOT be disabled" is still violable by any host with ordinary permissions, which is the outcome SEC-6 was filed against.

### GAP 3 — ISR + 24 h presigned GET is a real TOCTOU window

`apps/web/app/[slug]/page.tsx:61` is `export const revalidate = 60`, and `presignDisplayUrl` defaults to a 24-hour TTL (`apps/web/lib/uploads.ts:125`). The re-HEAD runs at *render*, not per guest request. Attacker replays the still-valid 5-minute presigned PUT after approval: the swapped bytes are served to every guest hitting the cached HTML for up to 60 s, and indefinitely (24 h) to anyone who already holds the emitted URL. Bounded, but the PR body's "the public read re-HEADs and compares" overstates it.

### GAP 4 — stale-by-bytes rows go permanently dark *and* invisible to admins

`verdictBindsMedia` is key-only, so after a byte swap `stdNsfwDisplayStatus` still returns `approved`. `stdVideoNeedsScreen` returns false (bound + decided) → never re-screened; `reveal-studio-surface.tsx:73` filters `s !== 'approved'` → never queued. Fail-closed, but unrecoverable without manual DB work.

---

## Attacks I tried and could NOT break (verified, not taken on trust)

I replayed the real migrations into PGlite reproducing the prod ordering (drop column → run `20271005100000` + `20271007100000` snapshots → run the new migration) and attacked as `SET ROLE authenticated`:

- `UPDATE … SET std_media_nsfw`, `… RETURNING`, `INSERT … (std_media_nsfw)`, `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET std_media_nsfw`, multi-column `SET (std_media, std_media_nsfw) = (…)`, `SET std_media_nsfw = DEFAULT`, `= NULL` → **all `permission denied for table events`**.
- **Non-vacuity proven independently**: after `GRANT UPDATE (std_media_nsfw) … TO authenticated`, the byte-identical statement **succeeds** and the forged verdict lands. The denial is the REVOKE, not a broken statement.
- No auto-updatable view exists in `public` (`pg_relation_is_updatable` = 0 for all); `std_media_nsfw` is exposed by exactly one relation (`events`).
- **0** SECURITY DEFINER functions containing dynamic SQL are executable by `authenticated`; **0** functions anywhere mention `std_media`. The one SECDEF function that updates `events` (`vendor_claim_locked_qr`) doesn't touch it. No trigger on `events` touches `std_media`.

## Regressions to legitimate behaviour

1. **The one live prod STD video goes dark immediately on migrate** (verdict deliberately not backfilled) with no user-facing notice. The PR body says it re-screens when "the couple opens their Save-the-Date builder **or an admin opens the Reveal Studio queue**" — **the admin half is false**: `fetchStdVideosNeedingReview` (`reveal-studio-surface.tsx:28-79`) never calls `screenStdVideo`. The only automatic heal is the couple's own builder visit (`save-the-date/page.tsx:155-161`). An admin must click Approve manually.
2. **Admin override tightened to refusal for poster-less videos** — `setStdVideoModeration` returns `no-poster`/`media-unreadable` (`apps/web/app/admin/reveal-studio/actions.ts:94-101`). Correct posture, but such rows sit in the queue with an un-actionable Approve button.
3. Rate/throttle: if `writeVerdict(pending)` ever fails to match (JSONB filter drift), `attemptedAt` never persists and every builder render re-loads the 4.4 MB model. Narrow, but unbounded when hit.

No regression to the couple's picker: `std_media` keeps its host UPDATE/SELECT grant (asserted in the migration post-condition and in the DB test), `fit`-only edits preserve the binding, and re-upload correctly invalidates + re-screens.

## Test quality: they enforce — not vacuous

- `apps/web/tests/db/std-media-nsfw-verdict.db.test.ts` — **the strongest DB test in this repo's style.** META asserts `current_user='authenticated'`, `rolbypassrls=false`, non-owner; two trap-probe columns prove the grant snapshot was actually reproduced (without them the harness's post-replay `GRANT ALL` would make every denial meaningless); every denial has a `service_role` differential; positive control proves `std_media` still writable. I re-derived non-vacuity independently by re-granting the column and watching the identical statement succeed. 9/9 pass. It also covers the INSERT vector, the anon vector, the legacy-key strip, no-backfill, and idempotency.
- `apps/web/lib/std-media.test.ts` — 19/19 pass, and the four neutralisations the implementer claims are plausible from the diff: `stdVideoIsLive → status==='approved'` breaks the six binding/fingerprint tests; `stdVerdictMatchesContent → true` breaks the three content tests; keeping the client `nsfw` key breaks `resolveStdMedia DROPS a client-supplied nsfw key`.
- **What the tests do not cover, and why the bugs got through:** every test uses well-formed `r2://setnayan-media/…` refs. There is no test for a non-`r2://` `videoKey`, and no test that the *serve* parser and the *verify* parser agree on a key. Add a property-style assertion that `parseStoredAsset(videoKey).kind === 'r2'` is a precondition of `stdVideoIsLive`, plus a case with `videoKey = 'http:/evil.example/x/uuid-clip.mp4'`. There is also no test that the screened poster is derived from the video (Bypass 2) — that one can't be tested until the product decides how to bind them (server-side frame extraction, or at minimum rejecting a `posterKey` not uploaded under the same event prefix).
